channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Chinese Robotics Suppliers Rise on Tesla Optimus Audit Report
item.description: Shares of Chinese robotics‑component suppliers climbed after a local report said Tesla Inc. teams had arrived in the country to audit suppliers and place additional orders to boost production of its Optimus humanoid model.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Waymo Plans to Offer Paid Robotaxi Rides in Singapore in 2028
item.description: Waymo plans to offer its robotaxi service in Singapore in 2028, the latest in a string of domestic and international expansions by the Alphabet Inc. unit.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Lung

item.title: Indian Project Financier’s Data Center Loans Top $1.2 Billion
item.description: India’s top state-run infrastructure financier has sanctioned loans upwards of 30 billion rupees ($313 million) each to at least four data centers, reflecting the nation’s push to participate in the artificial intelligence buildout.
item.dc:creator: Saikat Das and Divya Patil

item.title: Traders Eye Xi-Trump Meet for Clues on AI Rivalry, Yuan Outlook
item.description: Artificial intelligence, a lingering trade war and the yuan will likely dominate the agenda of the upcoming US-China summit, with focus on whether the two nations can reach concessions or put guardrails around key areas of competition, analysts say.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: India’s Quick-Commerce Architect Takes a Long Bet
item.description:
The man who transformed how urban India eats, dines, and shops, Deepinder Goyal built his food delivery startup Zomato into one of the country’s biggest consumer technology companies, Eternal. At the height of its success, Goyal stepped away from the day-to-day running of the company he built, to turn his attention to a very different set of challenges with a much longer horizon.
In an exclusive interview on his sprawling residence in Delhi, Bloomberg’s Haslinda Amin speaks with Goyal about the never-ending journeys of founders, his current pursuits, and his quest for a different kind of eternity. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: India’s Quick-Commerce Disruptor Stays Calm on AI ‘Myth’
item.description:
Widely seen as the architect of the instant delivery model in India, Deepinder Goyal stays confident that the platforms he has built up under Eternal, such as Zomato and Blinkit, can harness AI for their customers better than general AI models can.
As Goyal steps away from day-to-day operations of the company he has built, Bloomberg’s Haslinda Amin speaks with him in an exclusive interview from his sprawling private residence in Delhi, about his journey thus far and the pursuit of a different kind of eternity. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Palantir Hires Former UK Labour Veteran With NHS Deal in Limbo
item.description: Palantir Technologies Inc. has hired Tom Watson, a former Labour deputy leader, as a new executive in the UK, where it faces a barrage of criticism threatening a major contract.
item.dc:creator: Mark Bergen and Alex Morales

item.title: Pennsylvania Governor Shapiro Calls for Tougher AI Safeguards
item.description: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro called for tougher safeguards around artificial intelligence Thursday, wading into a growing debate over the risks of the rapidly advancing technology while arguing the US can continue to reap its economic benefits.
item.dc:creator: Liz Skalka

item.title: Stocks Rally as Yields Fall After the Fed Rate Hike
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are UBS US Rates Strategy Head Phoebe White, Cboe Global Markets VP, Head of Derivatives Market Intelligence Mandy Xu, Musician & FYI.AI Founder & CEO will.i.am, BNY Investments Chief Economist Vincent Reinhart, Charles Schwab Chief Investment Strategist Liz Ann Sonders, California Attorney General Rob Bonta, Macerich President & CEO Jack Hsieh, LuxExperience CEO Michael Kliger, & Jeni’s Splendid Ice Creams Founder Jeni Britton. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: LuxExperience CEO on Luxury Retail Customer Resiliency
item.description: Michael Kliger, CEO of LuxExperience, said the luxury market is becoming increasingly polarized, with affluent customers continuing to spend heavily while middle-class shoppers pull back under inflationary pressure. He said the company is less concerned about total active customers, which are around 900,000, than about growing the small group of top customers that generate a disproportionate share of sales. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Says Claude Drives 26% of Its Research and Development
item.description: More than a quarter of Anthropic PBC’s research and development work for artificial intelligence is driven by its Claude chatbot, according to the company, providing the clearest indication yet that AI can help speed up development of future models.
item.dc:creator: Shirin Ghaffary

item.title: Amazon Says AI Models Should Be Released When ‘Ready and Safe’
item.description: Amazon.com Inc. said artificial intelligence models should be released only after rigorous testing, weighing in on the debate about the pace of AI development after top labs called for a slowdown following safety lapses.
item.dc:creator: Matt Day

item.title: UN Must Unlock Its Doors to AI Industry: UNGA President
item.description: United Nations General Assembly president Khalilur Rahman speaks with Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick. This week United Nations Secretary General said nations must coordinate global efforts to regulate AI, echoing calls for closer monitoring of the technology after warnings from leaders of the world’s top firms. The comments come days before world leaders descend on New York for the UNGA’s annual high-level week. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: will.i.am on Personal AI Agents, Fundraising Efforts
item.description: Grammy-Award winning artist will.i.am sits down with Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick from Dreamforce to discuss his efforts to develop personal AI agents for college students, and the fundraising efforts around his company, FYI.AI (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Palantir CEO Says AI Firms Responsible for Their Own Actions
item.description: Palantir Technologies Inc. Chief Executive Officer Alex Karp said developers of artificial-intelligence systems need to be held liable for their own work as opposed to depending on government regulation.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Martin

item.title: SpaceX May Buy Data From Failed Startups for AI Models
item.description: Elon Musk’s SpaceX has held internal discussions about buying customer and operational information from troubled or defunct startups, according to people familiar with the matter. That data could help improve its artificial intelligence models. Ed Ludlow reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Four Big Deals That Reveal the State of Podcasting
item.description: New ventures involving ‘Giggly Squad,’ NPR, Steven Bartlett and Serial Productions have set the podcasting world atwitter
item.dc:creator: Ashley Carman

item.title: Anthropic's Warning of Existential Risk Hijacks Larger AI Debate
item.description: Some experts worry that heated rhetoric makes it hard to hold companies accountable, and sets back attempts to deal with environmental impact and job loss
item.dc:creator: Davey Alba and Rachel Metz

item.title: India’s Chip Plan Investment Pledges Hit $12 Billion
item.description: India has received investment pledges of as much as $12 billion from global and local investors within months of launching its new semiconductor policy, marking an acceleration in its efforts to become a chip-making nation.
item.dc:creator: Sankalp Phartiyal

item.title: Apple, OpenAI and Qualcomm Leaders to Attend Trump-Xi Dinner
item.description: Apple Inc. Executive Chairman Tim Cook, OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman and Qualcomm Inc. head Cristiano Amon are poised to attend a White House state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping next week.
item.dc:creator: Shirin Ghaffary, Mark Gurman and Ian King
